clue.text: Small drinking glass for £25

definitions.meaning: a small measure of beer or spirits, or the little glass it is served in
British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone pays a steep price for a tiny glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British usages: a little glass for a short measure, and money slang for twenty-five pounds.

clue.text: Solid girl in hollow must climb up

explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a pyramid is a solid figure on a polygonal base.

clue.text: Original volume written during Christmas

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: An author produced a fresh book over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means new and original.

clue.text: For example Marilyn Monroe's heavenly body

definitions.meaning: Monroe was a famous Hollywood leading lady, an example of a screen celebrity; the 's stands for 'is'
a sun seen shining in the night sky

explanation.surface: An admirer praises the actress's gorgeous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen celebrity and a shining sun in the night sky share the same word.

clue.text: Propositions that he's established only partly

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scholar's claims are only half proven.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward to be argued, and these are several.

clue.text: Suggestive of payment including benefit

indicators.note: including means holding inside

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A rent payment hints at state welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means evocative of, strongly reminding one of something.

clue.text: No time to destroy a wooden shoe

an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone has no time to wreck a wooden clog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' tells you to strip AGE from SABOTAGE, leaving the shoe; the word sabotage is said to come from such shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a clog carved from a single piece of wood, worn by French peasants.

clue.text: Blow about falling pound raised obstacle

parts.note: a sock is a punch, a blow
tumbling means falling

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for pound weight

explanation.surface: A blow sends the currency tumbling, holding the economy back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money falling in value; it is the weight abbreviation, and 'raised' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumbling block is a hindrance or obstacle.

clue.text: European bishop replacing unrefined person's verse

indicators.note: replacing says one letter is swapped in for another

parts.note: a vulgarian is a coarse, unrefined person
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman from the Continent rewrites a boor's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: B (bishop) takes the place of V (verse) in VULGARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bulgarian is a native of Bulgaria in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Friend supports small child without reservation

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter goes below

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely, wholly.

clue.text: Be an expert — and not just on alliaceous plants

definitions.text: Be an expert — and not just on alliaceous plants

parts.words: Be an expert — and not just on alliaceous plants
parts.note: an idiom for knowing your subject thoroughly, which literally names the bulbs of the garlic family

explanation.surface: A gardener is a specialist in more than just garlic and leeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to be thoroughly knowledgeable about something.

clue.text: Returns from flat in Parisian street

definitions.note: plural noun for income, matching a singular mass noun for takings

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: Someone earns rent from an apartment on a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment in the surface; here it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is the income a business or state takes in, its returns.

clue.text: Garment once worn at heart of battle?

definitions.text: Garment once worn at heart of battle?

parts.words: Garment once worn at heart of battle?
parts.note: a close-fitting jacket of Tudor times; also a pair of identical letters, as the TT in the middle of the word battle

explanation.surface: A historian describes armour-like clothing worn by soldiers in the thick of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a soldier's tunic; the cryptic reading looks at the word 'battle', whose middle is a repeated letter pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a man's close-fitting Renaissance jacket and a pair of identical things side by side.

clue.text: A revolutionary aid, currently, in the daily grind

definitions.text: A revolutionary aid, currently, in the daily grind

parts.words: A revolutionary aid, currently, in the daily grind
parts.note: something that turns ('revolutionary') driven by a stream's current, used every day to grind corn

explanation.surface: Something radical and modern helps with the tedium of ordinary working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests political upheaval and 'currently' the present day; here they mean turning round and powered by a water current.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-driven wheel turns the stones of a mill that grinds grain.

clue.text: Punch-up involving fine Scottish lads at first

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or handsome

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word lads

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out among fine young Scotsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough noisy fight, a punch-up.

clue.text: Turn out of bed and cut down to size?

to deflate someone's pretensions or expose a false claim

explanation.surface: Someone is roused from sleep and humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is jokey: DE- (removal) plus BUNK, a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose exaggerated claims is to deflate them; the punning reading removes someone from a berth.

clue.text: Carriers of poison in milk

definitions.meaning: the first milk a cow gives after calving

explanation.surface: Venom is found in the milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Beestings is the old word for colostrum; read as two words it names insects' venomous barbs.

clue.text: Boundlessness? I mostly encounter it in New York

indicators.note: in says these pieces are placed inside the next
mostly says the synonym for 'encounter' loses its last letter

parts.note: to find something is to come across or encounter it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the endless expanse is mostly what they meet in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encounter' must lose its last letter ('mostly') before joining 'it' inside New York's abbreviation; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinity is endlessness, a state without bounds or limits.

clue.text: Pain-killers freely distributed? Yes and no

indicators.note: freely distributed suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether painkillers are handed out freely and gets an equivocal reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodynes are medicines that relieve pain.

clue.text: Grace not so apparent in a male crooner

less means not so much

clue.text: Coarse material showing dollar sign

clue.text: Woman securing information for business schedule

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: Gold US investigators take time to raise

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or enlarge.

clue.text: Sort of chair quartet used, with adjustment to slew round

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

clue.text: Take someone's hand to become new partner

definitions.text: Take someone's hand to become new partner

parts.words: Take someone's hand to become new partner
parts.note: at a dance, interrupting a couple to take over as one person's partner

clue.text: Prosper in Gateshead, producing rods for cutting

taken as written

clue.text: A bit after Easter
